newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Foreign shareholder scores win at Russia steelmill.
newsitem.headline: Foreign shareholder scores win at Russia steelmill.

text.p: International investment fund Cambridge Capital Management (CCM) Limited scored a victory on Wednesday in a battle with Russian steelmaker Novolipetsk Metals Combine in a closely-watched dispute over shareholder rights.

A statement from Salomon Brothers, financial adviser to CCM on its Russia investment, said a regional arbitration court had ruled in CCM's favour -- the third such ruling in favour of an embattled foreign shareholder of the steelmill.

"We are very pleased with the court's decision which confirmed that our rights were grossly violated and sent a clear message that entrenched enterprise managers are not above Russian law," the statement quoted CCM chairman Thomas Gaffney as saying.
Novolipetsk's management had been seeking to block its foreign shareholders from winning seats on its board. Novolipetsk managers could not be reached for immediate comment.
Russian investment company Renaissance Capital and Russia's Bank MFK won similar legal victories earlier this month.
CCM owns 17.2 percent, MFK 15 percent and Renaissance investment arm Sputnik Funds nine percent in the steelmill.
The Novolipetsk case has been viewed as a barometer of the ability of foreign shareholders to win seats on boards at Russian enterprises under Russian law.
Russian securities and other laws are slowly taking shape but there are many loopholes and uncertainties.
